description: For string-type columns, avoid copying field data entirely by producing offset-length pairs that point directly into the memory-mapped input buffer. Fields that don't require unescaping (no embedded quotes) can be served as zero-copy slices, while only the ~5-10% of fields requiring unescape get copied into a separate buffer. This leverages the observation that most CSV fields are simple unquoted values.
mathematical_formalization: Let F_total = total fields, F_escape = fields requiring unescape. Copy cost: C_full = F_total * avg_field_len * C_memcpy. Zero-copy cost: C_zero = F_escape * avg_escaped_field_len * C_memcpy + F_total * C_offset_store. Speedup: C_full / C_zero = F_total * avg_len / (F_escape * avg_escaped_len + F_total * sizeof(offset)). When F_escape / F_total < 10%, speedup approaches avg_len / sizeof(offset) ~ 10-50x for field extraction.
analogical_connections: Linux sendfile / splice: zero-copy network I/O avoids kernel-userspace copies, same principle of avoiding unnecessary data movement
Database late materialization: only materialize column values when actually needed by the query, minimizing data movement
Memory-mapped file I/O: mmap lets the OS manage page caching while the parser operates directly on virtual memory addresses
implementation_hypothesis: mmap the input file. Phase 1 produces an index of (offset, length, needs_unescape) tuples. For fields where needs_unescape=false, return &input[offset..offset+length] directly. For escaped fields, copy to an escape buffer while removing doubled quotes. Use the 'needs_unescape' flag from the quote-pairing stage (a field needs unescaping only if it contains '""' inside quotes).
experiment_seed: Profile memory bandwidth and throughput on a 5GB CSV file with 5%, 20%, 50% fields requiring unescape. Measure: (1) memory copy bytes saved, (2) parsing throughput improvement, (3) RSS memory usage. Compare mmap vs. read-based I/O for Phase 1 scanning.
